title: Leveraging Pedagogical Theories to Understand Student Learning Process with Graph-based Reasonable Knowledge Tracing

problem.claim: Knowledge tracing aims to predict student performance while tracking evolving knowledge.

gap.claim: Many deep-learning knowledge tracing methods prioritize predictive accuracy but do not explicitly model dynamic knowledge mastery or produce results that educators can readily comprehend and apply.

contributions.claim: The authors conduct a preliminary analysis of mainstream knowledge tracing approaches to identify and explain unreasonable behavior.
The authors introduce GRKT, a graph-based reasonable knowledge tracing method that models mutual influences among knowledge concepts.
The method uses a fine-grained psychological three-stage process covering knowledge retrieval, memory strengthening, and knowledge learning or forgetting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that GRKT outperforms eleven baselines across three datasets in predictive accuracy and produces more reasonable knowledge tracing results.
The authors describe GRKT as promising for practical implementation in educational settings.
The authors report that source code is available in a GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Knowledge tracing predicts student performance to track evolving knowledge.
Deep-learning approaches emphasize predictive accuracy but may fail to represent knowledge mastery processes or produce educator-comprehensible results.
The authors analyze mainstream approaches and introduce GRKT.
GRKT models concept interactions with graph neural networks and uses a three-stage psychological learning process.
The authors report improvements over eleven baselines across three datasets and potential educational applicability.

source_observation.claim: The abstract identifies a tension between predictive accuracy and tracking knowledge mastery in an interpretable, educationally usable way.

interpretation.claim: Educational prediction systems may need evaluation criteria that address process representation and reasonableness alongside predictive performance.

application.claim: When designing knowledge tracing systems, assess whether model outputs correspond to an intelligible account of learning dynamics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how reasonableness is operationalized or evaluated.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the three datasets or eleven baselines.
Evaluation metrics and experimental protocol are unspecified.
The operational definition and validation procedure for reasonable tracing are unspecified.
Model architecture details and limitations are omitted.
